title: Benefit Authorization and Limits for Real Estate Service Contract Claims
content:
## Authority to authorize

A benefit under a Real Estate Service Contracts plan is authorized only after a covered determination is on file for the service request, as shown by that request's claim records. Only one repair, replacement or cash-in-lieu authorization is open per service request. An authorization is reversed in full when the work will not be performed and never after completion.

## Repair or replacement

Bridgewell chooses repair or replacement: it replaces when the repair estimate is at or above the plan's repair-to-replace threshold times the contracted replacement cost, when parts cannot be obtained within the plan's parts lead time in calendar days, or when the item cannot be repaired, and otherwise repairs. The work's cost is the repair estimate when Bridgewell repairs and the contracted replacement cost when it replaces.

## Amount paid

- **Seller phase.** The amount paid is the lowest of the work's cost, the plan's per-item seller limit less the seller-phase benefit already paid on the same item, and the plan's total seller limit less the seller-phase benefit paid on the order, and never below zero. The seller-phase sums run over the whole seller listing coverage period of the order, net of reversals.
- **Buyer phase.** The amount paid is the lowest of the work's cost, the item's limit less the benefit paid on that item in the contract year (allowances excluded), and the plan's total contract-year limit less the buyer-phase benefit paid in the contract year, and never below zero. Buyer limits apply per contract year and restart on each anniversary of the coverage start date: contract years are consecutive 12-month periods starting on the coverage start date, and a request belongs to the contract year in which its request date falls. Benefit paid is counted net of reversals.

The item's limit is the plan's limit for that item: heating system, cooling system, ductwork, plumbing, water heater, electrical, kitchen appliance, laundry appliance, garage door opener or roof leak.

## Allowances, cash in lieu and rekeying

- Buyer-phase supplemental allowances (code violation; permit; haul-away on a replacement; refrigerant on a cooling repair) pay the lower of the documented invoice amount and the allowance, with refrigerant limited per contract year by the refrigerant allowance already paid in that contract year, and count toward the aggregate limit only; the seller phase carries no allowances.
- When a like unit cannot be sourced, or the buyer asks for cash in place of an authorized replacement, cash in lieu equal to the contracted replacement cost within the same limits is offered, and is authorized when the buyer accepts it no later than the plan's cash-in-lieu offer validity, in calendar days, after the offer. An accepted cash settlement replaces the replacement authorization, which is reversed in full, and is paid within the plan's cash-in-lieu payment period in calendar days.
- The rekey benefit is authorized at the contracted locksmith cost and counts toward the aggregate limit only.

The plan's benefit consumed is the dollars Bridgewell has committed toward covered repairs, replacements, cash in lieu and rekeying on the contract, net of reversals.

## Worked example (hypothetical buyer-phase request)

A hypothetical plan with a heating system limit of $2500.00, a total contract-year limit of $12000.00 and a repair-to-replace threshold of 60%. Earlier in the same contract year, $1000.00 has been paid on the heating system and $3000.00 in total. The new heating failure has a repair estimate of $2000.00 and a contracted replacement cost of $3000.00.
1. 60% of $3000.00 is $1800.00; the estimate of $2000.00 is at or above it, so Bridgewell replaces, and the work's cost is $3000.00.
2. Item room: $2500.00 less $1000.00 is $1500.00.
3. Aggregate room: $12000.00 less $3000.00 is $9000.00.
4. The lowest of $3000.00, $1500.00 and $9000.00 is $1500.00, the amount paid.
